sermon.title: Answer Two Bible Questions 02/18/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer explains Jeremiah’s question “what is the chaff to the wheat?” with a threshing-floor illustration: chaff is wrong belief that stops growth. Jesus’ baptism of fire, like a refiner’s fire and hammer, burns it away. He lists doctrines he considers chaff and says people can’t judge what is right until this fire opens their understanding.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A congregant’s name is in the transcript only. Kept as spoken: “Jeremiah 26 28” (later “23 28,” correct); “Exodus three to” (3:2). Points to check: Obama and George W. Bush both said publicly the Bible approves slavery, and he wrote both (24:07); 12-step programs “less than seven percent” (42:00); civil leaders are God’s “third largest topic.” Sensitive content kept as spoken: Calvinist predestination, once saved always saved, Jesus-only, pre-tribulation rapture; Catholic idols, holy water, sign of the cross; Orthodox icons; name-it-claim-it; socialism and the Democratic party; liberal churches; angels have no sexual organs; women keep silent “that’s bunk.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the Angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. So he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.

But Moses said to God, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?” So He said, “I will certainly be with you. And this shall be a sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
